definitions.explanation: The underground part of a plant that absorbs water and nutrients. Slightly informal/colloquial.

examples.japanese: {木|き}の{根|ね}っこが{土|つち}から{出|で}ている。
examples.english: The roots of the tree are sticking out of the ground.

examples.japanese: {根|ね}っこから{引|ひ}き{抜|ぬ}いた。
examples.english: I pulled it out from the root.

examples.japanese: {雑草|ざっそう}の{根|ね}っこを{取|と}る。
examples.english: I remove the roots of the weeds.

notes:
{根|ね}っこ is a colloquial term for the root of a plant.

WORD FORMATION:
{根|ね} (root) + っこ (diminutive/casual suffix)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {根|ね}っこから{引|ひ}き{抜|ぬ}く: to pull out from the root
- {根|ね}っこを{取|と}る: to remove the roots
- {木|き}の{根|ね}っこ: tree roots

REGISTER:
Slightly informal/colloquial. Use {根|ね} in more formal contexts.

RELATED WORDS:
- {根|ね}: root (standard)
- {根元|ねもと}: base, root area
- {根|ね}を{張|は}る: to take root (figurative)

FIGURATIVE USE:
Can imply the fundamental/deep-rooted part: {問題|もんだい}の{根|ね}っこ (the root of a problem).
